MMseqs2, three rounds
Tool id mmseqs2_iterative. Numbers from seanome/2024-kmerseek-analysis commit 4a4b1171.
What it compares
A profile of a protein family, built by MMseqs2 from its own hits over three rounds of search, as jackhmmer does.
What it needs
sequence only: yes
3D structure prediction: no
GPU: no
Reference searched
The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as an MMseqs2 database.
How to read its score
Bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
Strong and weak strata

Under the Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, its best setting is s7: Fmax 0.324 over 2,435 true instances. Below, each stratum compares this setting with the best setting of any other tool in that same stratum, so the other tool's setting can change from line to line. Only strata with at least 30 true instances are compared.
Where it is closest to, or furthest ahead of, the best other tool:
identity 30–40% to the closest same-family domain: Fmax 0.209 (n = 165); best other: phmmer default, 0.199.
AlphaFold confidence (pLDDT) 90–100: Fmax 0.484 (n = 186); best other: MMseqs2 s7, 0.480.
Where it is furthest behind the best other tool:
regions 16–30 aa long: Fmax 0.028 (n = 271); best other: kmerseek wwmj5_k11_lcFalse, 0.330.
regions 31–60 aa long: Fmax 0.085 (n = 420); best other: kmerseek gbmr4_k21_lcFalse, 0.232.
Swiss-Prot features, raw calls, zebrafish, setting s7: best feature type DOMAIN (domain), Fmax 0.321 (n = 1,107); worst MOTIF (short motif), Fmax 0.004 (n = 190).
Known failure modes
At most 1,000 target proteins are kept per query (--max-seqs 1000). How often that cut hits: not measured.
Each round can pull in proteins from a different family. How often: not measured.
Cost per 1,000 queries

Setting s7, searching one relative (mean over the 15 relatives it searched): 0.0787 core-hours reserved per 1,000 queries (16 cores for the task's wall time), measured on Sherlock. Peak memory 1.1 GB. That is about $0.00351 at $0.044625 per CPU-hour. Building its databases took 0.00889 core-hours over 7 databases. A database is built once and reused, so this is not in the per-query cost.
The per-query cost counts the search only. The run recorded cost per tool and setting, summed over all relatives, so the cost for one relative is the mean.
Hardware

Hardware of the search (setting s7, every task): Sherlock partition hns, from the trace. Host name: not recorded in the trace, so the node is the one SLURM's job record (sacct) gives. 15 tasks on 8 nodes. CPU: AMD 9754 (6 tasks); AMD 7543 (5 tasks); AMD 8224P (4 tasks). GPU: none allocated.

Hardware of the database build: Sherlock partition hns, from the trace. Host name: not recorded in the trace, so the node is the one SLURM's job record (sacct) gives. 7 tasks on 5 nodes. CPU: AMD 8224P (3 tasks); AMD 7543 (1 task); AMD 7742 (1 task); AMD 9754 (1 task); not recorded, as scontrol no longer finds the node (1 task). GPU: none allocated.

Sources, read 2026-10-16: the partition is the queue column of the run's Nextflow traces. The traces have no hostname column, so the node is the one SLURM's job record (sacct) gives for the trace's job id. CPU and GPU are that node's features in SLURM (scontrol show node: CPU_MNF, CPU_SKU, GPU_SKU), named as on Sherlock's node features page. Partition hns is owned by a research group, and Sherlock's tech specs page lists no CPU models for such partitions. Script: scripts/read_hardware.py.
Licence
Licence: MIT (source)
Commercial use allowed: Yes.
Settings in the table
s7: sensitivity 7 (-s 7), three rounds
Version, container, command
Version: MMseqs2 18.8cc5c
Container: quay.io/biocontainers/mmseqs2:18.8cc5c--hd6d6fdc_0 (sha256:3503bfe576d560e550df2872af86a1ad1bcc1c06cfb7caadd3e7a95649f5f0ef)
mmseqs search \ human-38fdd87d_mmdb/db zebrafish_mmdb/db result mmseqs_tmp \ --threads 16 \ -s 7 \ --num-iterations 3 \ --max-seqs 1000 \ -e 10.0
Followed by mmseqs convertalis to write the table of hits.
Will it work for you?

Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.241 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.300 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.337 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.209 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting s7; strata with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.245 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.319 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.462 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.028 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.085 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting s7.)
Can you spend about 0.0787 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" above.
